what: Chained INT3 sampler: works at idle, still not survivable across AT&T8
board: 20.16 MHz Courier V.Everything, ID_SDL v4.03d, supervisor 7.4.16, DSP 3.1.2

what works.chaining: The handler saves AX/BX/DS, samples, restores and `jmp far 8000:0a77`, leaving the interrupt frame untouched so the firmware's own handler runs normally and owns the EOI and the iret. At idle this is stable and the ring fills.
what works.measured tick: INT3 runs at ~303 Hz - the pointer advanced 0x4028 -> 0x44e4 -> 0x49a0 over three seconds
what works.atomic arming: Masking INT3 across the vector swap was tried and reset the board: the firmware cannot lose its tick for the third of a second two commands take. The swap is instead made atomic by changing only the SEGMENT word, leaving the offset at 0x0a77 and placing the handler at (segment << 4) + 0x0a77. One command arms, one disarms, and there is no intermediate state.

what does not work: Armed across AT&T8 the board still resets, and the cause is not yet known. Ruled out along the way: the extra EOI (chained version issues none), interrupt latency (a lean push AX/BX/DS handler fails the same way), the port reads (a --ports none build fails), the handler's work entirely (a bare 5-byte `jmp far` stub fails), and placement in &T8-cleared RAM (relocating to 0x1a77, which &T8 leaves alone, fails the same way).

the big finding.claim: AT&T8 zeroes 0x3000-0x8000 and writes 0x55 at 0x2c00, 0x9000 and 0xa000.
the big finding.method: markers written across low RAM, &T8 run with NOTHING armed, markers read back
the big finding.why it matters: The surveyed-free 20 KiB block at 0x2e00-0x7eff, where every probe in this repository is placed, is mostly erased by &T8. A takeover probe does not care - it runs and dies inside the watchdog's 1.6 s. Anything co-resident with the firmware is destroyed mid-run. docs/ram-probe-delivery.md warned that 'zero is not the same as unused'; this is that warning coming true, in the other direction - the region is not merely used, it is actively cleared.

correction to coop-loadonly-01: Its conclusion 'it is the interrupt, not the port reads' still holds, but the mechanism it proposed - the non-specific EOI - is now ruled out, and so is every other mechanism tried since. The cause is open.
mistake worth recording: A full (non --assume-zero) placement at 0x1a00 wrote zeros over a live firmware data block at 0x1aab-0x1ad6 that the region scan had already identified. The modem kept answering AT/ATI3/ATI7 normally and the next reset cleared it anyway, but the write was avoidable: the image spans a whole 512-byte page and only 52 bytes of it are code.
